intent: Test whether widening the outer sensors to ±0.045 m reduces slalom line losses and lifts slalom progress, while keeping the iteration 5 drivetrain (track 0.10 m, radius 0.040 m, mass 0.5 kg). Expected result: slalom line_loss_events drop below 1.85 and slalom progress rises above 0.14. Oval finish rate should stay at or near 95%. If the oval finish rate falls, the wider spread is adding steering lag, and the best design reverts to iteration 5.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) Outer sensors at ±0.045 m reduce slalom line_loss_events below 1.85, because the outer sensors keep seeing tape to about 0.0655 m offset. (2) Oval finish rate stays at or above 90%. If it falls while slalom does not improve, spread is not the slalom limit and the next step is a forward offset change, not more spread. (3) If steering_oscillation rises without a max_error change, the Integrator should retune gains. (4) Track 0.09 m (iteration 7) is ruled out: it cut the oval finish rate and s-bend progress, so the track stays at 0.10 m.
rationale:
Evidence from the development race history:
- Iteration 5 (5 sensors at y=0.07 m, 16 mm footprint, track 0.10 m, radius 0.040 m, mass 0.5 kg) is the best design at 422.9. Its oval finish rate is 95%, and its s-bend progress is 0.72.
- Iteration 6 (mass 0.4 kg) scored about the same (422.1). Oval held, but s-bend progress fell to 0.59. Mass 0.5 kg is the better operating point.
- Iteration 7 (track 0.09 m) scored 347. The oval finish rate fell from 95% to 60% and s-bend progress fell to 0.57. Narrowing the track adds turn authority but also oscillation and overshoot, so I revert it to 0.10 m.

The remaining gap is slalom. It has about 0.14 progress and about 1.85 line-loss events per run. Its failures look like sensor coverage on alternating bends: the outer sensors lose the tape at about 0.0565 m offset, which is close to the 0.06 m off-track limit. Iteration 3 showed that adding sensor spread alongside forward look-ahead at y=0.08 m overshoots and hurts the oval. Iteration 1 widened the spread at y=0.04 m with a 12 mm footprint, and that did not help. This iteration therefore changes only the outer spread, from ±0.036 m to ±0.045 m, with 5 sensors at 0.0225 m pitch and the same 16 mm footprint and y=0.07 m. Outer coverage rises to about 0.0655 m offset. All other values stay at the iteration 5 settings, so this is a one-variable test against iteration 5.
